original_question: An n-dimensional simplex is called empty when its intersection with the integer lattice Z^n consists exactly of its vertices. Classify all empty simplices of dimension n up to affine integer-lattice congruence.
target_in_paper: Section 3.2, Problem 4: the paper asks for a classification of empty simplices of dimension n up to lattice congruence, in the discussion of faces of sails and as a generalization of White’s theorem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper’s core content almost exactly: it uses the correct emptiness condition (intersection with Z^n equals the vertices) and asks for classification up to affine lattice-preserving equivalence, which is the paper’s notion of integer/lattice congruence. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))
missing_details: The ambient setting should be stated explicitly: an n-dimensional simplex in the real vector space R^n with respect to the standard lattice Z^n. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))

It should be made explicit that one is classifying lattice simplices, i.e. simplices whose vertices are lattice points; in the paper, emptiness is defined by requiring that the lattice points of the simplex are exactly its vertices. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))

The equivalence relation should be tied to Definition 1.1: integer congruence/lattice congruence means equivalence under an affine transformation of R^n that preserves Z^n. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))
The quantifier on n should be explicit: the problem is posed dimension-by-dimension for a fixed positive integer n. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))

If you want the question to reflect the paper’s research-status framing, you should note that the text immediately after Problem 4 records the already understood low-dimensional cases and presents the higher-dimensional cases as the open part. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))
refined_question: For a fixed positive integer n, classify up to integer congruence all empty lattice n-simplices Δ ⊂ R^n; that is, all n-dimensional simplices with vertices in Z^n such that Δ ∩ Z^n is exactly the vertex set of Δ, where integer congruence means equivalence under affine automorphisms of R^n preserving Z^n. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))
justification: This is clearly Problem 4 in Section 3.2, not a broader neighboring question: the draft reproduces the paper’s empty-simplex classification problem, while Definition 1.1 supplies the exact meaning of the congruence relation used there. The surrounding paragraph in Section 3.2 also explains that this is being posed as a higher-dimensional extension of White’s theorem, so the refined version should stay narrowly focused on empty lattice simplices and integer congruence rather than drifting to more general lattice polytopes or sail faces. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1712.01450))
